name: Thinking Machines Lab
summary: Mira Murati's AI lab is building collaborative, multimodal AI systems and raised a record $2B seed round at a reported $12B valuation.
overview: Thinking Machines Lab is an AI research and product company founded by former OpenAI chief technology officer Mira Murati. It is pursuing multimodal systems designed for collaborative use and customization.

bull_case: An experienced frontier-AI team, unusually large initial financing, and a focus on customization could establish a credible alternative to the largest model labs.
bear_case: The company must turn research talent and capital into differentiated products while competing with better-resourced incumbents and fast-moving open models.

intelligence.description: Thinking Machines Lab is an AI research and product company developing collaborative, multimodal systems with an emphasis on customization.
company: Thinking Machines Lab was founded in 2025 by Mira Murati and a group of former OpenAI researchers and leaders. Its stated ambition is to build multimodal AI that works naturally with people and supports collaborative use, rather than focusing solely on a single consumer assistant.

The company closed a reported $2 billion seed round in July 2025 at a $12 billion valuation. In 2026 it released Inkling, an open-weight model positioned around customization, giving outside observers an early product signal after its initial research-focused period.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Thinking Machines Lab shows how investors are valuing founder quality, research talent, and AI optionality before a mature commercial business exists. Its progress is relevant to the competitive structure of frontier models, open-weight distribution, and the economics of building a new AI lab.

changed.text: Mira Murati introduces Thinking Machines Lab and its collaborative-AI mission.
The company closes a reported $2B seed round at a $12B valuation.
Thinking Machines releases Inkling, providing its first visible product and model-distribution signal.

takeaways: The reported $12B valuation reflects investor confidence in the team and research opportunity more than a mature revenue base.
Inkling gives the company an early test of its customization thesis and developer distribution strategy.
Competing for frontier talent and compute remains expensive, even after a record-sized seed round.
The most important proof point is whether products build durable user and enterprise demand beyond attention to the founding team.
